title: What Is Art Deco and Why Is It Popular Again?
titleZh: 什么是装饰艺术风格?它为何再度流行?
credits: Kim Cook reported on this story for the Associated Press. John Russell adapted it for VOA Learning English.

sentences.en: Art Deco is an international artistic style that was popular in the 1920s and 1930s.
sentences.zh: 装饰艺术是一种在20世纪20年代和30年代流行的国际艺术风格。

sentences.en: Now, interest in the style and its qualities is growing.
sentences.zh: 如今，人们对这种风格及其特质的兴趣正在增长。

sentences.en: A new generation is enjoying the style’s roots and turning it into something new.
sentences.zh: 新一代人正在欣赏这种风格的根源，并将其转化为全新的东西。

sentences.en: A public showing, or exhibition, at the Museum of the City of New York provides a look at the style that helped define the city 100 years ago.
sentences.zh: 纽约市博物馆举办的一场公开展览，让人们得以一睹这种在100年前帮助塑造这座城市的面貌的风格。

sentences.en: Famous Art Deco buildings include the Chrysler Building, the Empire State Building, Rockefeller Center and Radio City Music Hall.
sentences.zh: 著名的装饰艺术建筑包括克莱斯勒大厦、帝国大厦、洛克菲勒中心和无线电城音乐厅。

sentences.en: The public showing, called “Art Deco City: New York Postcards from the Leonard A.
sentences.zh: 这场名为“艺术装饰城市：伦纳德·A.

sentences.en: Lauder Collection,” also has clothing and film clips from the time.
sentences.zh: 劳德收藏”的公开展览，还展出了那个时代的服装和影片片段。

sentences.en: In London, the Victoria and Albert Museum has a collection of day and evening clothing, jewelry and more.
sentences.zh: 在伦敦，维多利亚与阿尔伯特博物馆收藏了日间和晚间服装、珠宝等物品。

sentences.en: The collection comes from Les Ballets Russes, a dance company that had a major effect on fashion.
sentences.zh: 这些藏品来自俄罗斯芭蕾舞团，这是一支对时尚产生过重大影响的舞蹈团体。

sentences.en: And in Paris, organizers of the 2024 Olympics created Art Deco posters last year to celebrate the games and mark the one hundred years since the 1924 Olympics, which Paris also hosted.
sentences.zh: 在巴黎，2024年奥运会的 organizers 去年创作了装饰艺术海报，以庆祝奥运会并纪念1924年奥运会一百周年，巴黎也曾举办过那届奥运会。

sentences.en: Experts have different opinions about Art Deco.
sentences.zh: 专家们对装饰艺术有着不同的看法。

sentences.en: Design writer Arricca Elin Sansone, for example, said last year in Elle Décor magazine: “Ask three historians to define the term Art Deco, and you’ll likely get three varying answers.”
sentences.zh: 设计作家阿里卡·埃林·桑森举例说，去年她在《ELLE DECOR》杂志上写道：“若请三位历史学家来定义‘艺术装饰’这一术语，你很可能得到三种不同的答案。”

sentences.en: Appearing after World War I, the first Art Deco era had a spirit of creativity and freedom.
sentences.zh: 装饰艺术出现在第一次世界大战之后，第一个装饰艺术时代充满了创造力和自由的精神。

sentences.en: With the aim of appearing modern, the style became one of the most important forms of design in the 1920s and early 1930s.
sentences.zh: 为了显得现代化，这种风格在20世纪20年代和30年代初成为最重要的设计形式之一。

sentences.en: The Art Deco style is believed to have first appeared at the 1925 International Exhibition of Modern Decorative and Industrial Arts, in Paris.
sentences.zh: 人们认为，装饰艺术风格首次亮相于1925年在巴黎举办的现代装饰与工业艺术国际博览会。

sentences.en: The early 1930s saw the development of the style in Miami where South Beach’s Art Deco District is popular with visitors and a center for design.
sentences.zh: 20世纪30年代初，这种风格在迈阿密得到发展，那里南海滩的装饰艺术区深受游客喜爱，也是设计的中心。

sentences.en: In some large cities, low-rise buildings of two or three floors turned into landscapes of high-rise skyscrapers.
sentences.zh: 在一些大城市，两三层低矮的楼房变成了高层摩天大楼的景观。

sentences.en: Public and private spaces showed themes involving geometrical designs and luxurious materials.
sentences.zh: 公共和私人空间展现出涉及几何图案和奢华材料的主题。

sentences.en: In transportation, faster cars and better trains suggested a new age while jazz music urged people to celebrate.
sentences.zh: 在交通方面，更快的汽车和更好的火车预示着一个新时代的到来，而爵士乐则激励着人们去庆祝。

sentences.en: The same energy can be found in today’s fashion shows and red-carpet events for stars.
sentences.zh: 同样的活力也能在当今的时装秀和明星的红毯活动中找到。

sentences.en: Some of today’s colorful clothing suggests the Jazz Age, another name for the period when Art Deco was popular.
sentences.zh: 当今一些色彩斑斓的服装让人联想到爵士时代，这是装饰艺术盛行的另一个名称。

sentences.en: Stars like Zendaya, Gigi Hadid, Beyoncé and Demi Lovato have used elements of the Deco era in new ways.
sentences.zh: 赞达亚、吉吉·哈迪德、碧昂丝和黛米·洛瓦托等明星以新的方式使用了装饰艺术时代的元素。

sentences.en: “The aesthetic of the 1920s is enjoying a fashionable renaissance,” said Kirsty Thatcher of the Australian fashion magazine Russh.
sentences.zh: 澳大利亚时尚杂志《拉什》的克斯蒂·撒切尔说：“20世纪20年代的美学正经历一场时尚的复兴。”

sentences.en: A “renaissance” represents a rebirth of something from the past.
sentences.zh: “复兴”代表着对过去某种事物的重生。

sentences.en: New York-based interior designer Vanessa DeLeon told the Associated Press, “The boldness and elegance of Art Deco are what appeals to me.”
sentences.zh: 总部位于纽约的室内设计师瓦妮莎·德莱昂告诉美联社：“装饰艺术的大胆与优雅正是吸引我的地方。”

sentences.en: Jamie Watkins and Tom Kennedy of the London design company Divine Savages include Art Deco elements in their collections of products for the home.
sentences.zh: 伦敦设计公司Divine Savages的杰米·沃特金斯和汤姆·肯尼迪在他们的家居产品系列中融入了装饰艺术元素。

sentences.en: Watkins suggested: “It’s no wonder we’re drawn to it again.”
sentences.zh: 沃特金斯建议：“难怪我们会再次被它吸引。”

sentences.en: Lynda Klich is the co-organizer or curator of the exhibition at the Museum of the City of New York.
sentences.zh: 琳达·克利希是纽约市博物馆此次展览的共同组织者或策展人。

sentences.en: Klich noted that postcards were the social media of their day.
sentences.zh: 克利希指出，明信片曾是那个时代的社交媒体。

sentences.en: Travelers at the time busily wrote messages to friends and family.
sentences.zh: 当时的旅行者忙着向亲友撰写信息。

sentences.en: New York’s famous Art Deco buildings appear in over 250 postcards.
sentences.zh: 纽约著名的装饰艺术建筑出现在250多张明信片中。

sentences.en: There is also a selection of clothing from the 1920s, shoes and other objects.
sentences.zh: 此外还有一批20世纪20年代的服装、鞋子及其他物品。

sentences.en: “Art Deco was the look that sold the city to the world,” said co-curator Lilly Tuttle.
sentences.zh: 共同策展人莉莉·图特尔说：“装饰艺术是这座城市向全世界推销的形象。”

sentences.en: The exhibition in New York City runs through February 17.
sentences.zh: 此次在纽约市举办的展览将持续到2月17日。

sentences.en: I’m John Russell.
sentences.zh: 我是约翰·拉塞尔。

glossary.def: a particular form of design that is repeated through a period because it is popular
glossary.zh: 特定设计风格；流行样式

to have or show differences between items or things
